tool.task.create.description: Create an AI delivery task: initializes task.json/stages.json/context.md/questions.json/artifacts/ etc. (PRD 7.1 / 8.1.1). Auto-detects task_type when not specified.
tool.task.create.title: Task title
tool.task.create.description.arg: Task description (used to detect task type)
tool.task.create.task_type: Task type (default auto-detect): crud / lightweight_ddd / full_ddd / analysis / bug_fix
tool.task.create.assignees: Task-level assignment: role -> assignee email (each role has exactly one assignee per task; optional; unassigned roles are confirmed by the user from candidates on stage advance)
tool.task.create.skip_stages: Stage names to skip (optional); these stages will be marked as skipped
tool.task.create.config_required: First use requires configuration first: {missing}. Please configure via the corresponding tools before creating a task.
tool.task.create.need_team: team.set (team roster, at least one member)
tool.task.create.view_hint: New task created. View in browser: {url}
tool.task.assign.description: Set the assignee for a task role (role -> member email; each role has exactly one assignee per task; repeated calls overwrite the previous assignee). Used to confirm the user's choice after stage advance, or to change an assignee anytime.
tool.task.get.description: Get task details: basic info, stages, artifact summary, pending questions (PRD 8.1.2 / 9.2).
tool.task.role_candidates.description: Query candidate assignees for a task role: returns all team members holding that role, plus the current assignee for this task (if any). Used to present options to the user after stage advance, or before changing an assignee.
tool.task.role_candidates.hint_assigned: Role {role} is assigned to {name} ({email}) in this task; call task.assign to change it.
tool.task.role_candidates.hint_unassigne: Role {role} has no assignee in this task yet; let the user pick from the candidates, then call task.assign to fix it.
tool.task.delete.description: Delete a task (PRD 8.1.2 extension): permanently deletes the tasks/{task_id}/ directory (task.json/stages.json/context.md/questions.json/artifacts/gates/delivery_package). Not recoverable. Requires explicit confirmation confirmed_by=true to prevent accidental deletion.
tool.task.delete.confirmed_by: Confirm deletion (must be true to prevent accidental deletion). Deletion is not recoverable; confirm with the user first.
tool.task.delete.confirmation_required: Deleting a task requires explicit confirmation: confirmed_by=true. Deletion is not recoverable; confirm with the user first.
tool.task.detect_type.description: Detect task type and recommend a flow (PRD 7.2 / 8.2 / 9.3).
tool.task.get_flow.description: Get the flow template for a task type (PRD 9.4).
tool.task.export_delivery_package.descri: Export the full delivery package delivery_package.md (PRD 7.10 / 8.9 / 9.15). Exportable only after all required stages complete. Optional format: md / html / both (default md); html is a self-contained single file for sharing.
tool.task.export_delivery_package.format: Export format (default md): md / html / both
tool.stage.get.description: Get stage status and readiness: can_start, missing upstream artifacts, assigned Agent, blocking questions (PRD 7.3 / 7.4 / 8.4).
tool.stage.complete.description: Mark a stage as complete (PRD 7.7 / 8.4 / 9.6). Prerequisites: 1) required artifacts exist 2) artifact status validated 3) gate.check passed 4) no open blocking questions in the task (regardless of which stage they block). Stage completion must be confirmed by the user (confirmed_by). Advances current_stage on completion.
tool.stage.complete.confirmed_by: User confirming person (name/email); user confirmation required before completing the stage
tool.stage.complete.artifact_not_validat: Artifacts not passed gate: {items}. Run gate.check first.
tool.stage.complete.gate_not_passed: Artifact {type} has not passed gate ({result}). Run gate.check first.
tool.stage.complete.blocked_by_question: Task has unresolved blocking questions (affecting stages: {stages}): {questions}
tool.stage.complete.view_hint: Stage advanced. View task in browser: {url}
tool.stage.complete.assignment_hint: The next stage {stage} (role {role}) has no fixed assignee yet. Present the candidates ({candidates}) to the user, let the user choose, then call task.assign to fix it.
tool.artifact.submit.description: Submit an artifact: saves the Markdown file and creates metadata (PRD 7.5 / 9.7). Validates upstream stage completion before submit (PRD 7.3 double check).
tool.artifact.submit.title: Artifact title
tool.artifact.submit.unexpected_type: Artifact type {type} does not belong to stage {stage}
tool.artifact.submit.artifact_exists: Stage {stage} already has {type} ({id} v{version}); use artifact.update to revise
tool.artifact.list.description: List task artifacts (PRD 9.9), optionally filtered by stage.
tool.artifact.update.description: Revise an artifact: keeps history (PRD 14.4 / 12.3 rework flow), version +1, status back to submitted.
tool.gate.check.description: Run gate check on a stage artifact (PRD 7.6 / 9.10). Pass -> artifact validated / stage validated; fail -> needs_revision. Result recorded to gates/{stage}.gate.json (PRD 14.3).
tool.gate.check.artifact_stage_mismatch: Artifact {id} does not belong to stage {stage}
tool.context.get_shared.description: Read the task shared context context.md (PRD 7.8 / 9.11): project background, business rules, unified language, confirmed decisions, pending questions, etc.
tool.context.get_project_background.desc: Get the project background (project-level, shared across tasks: business domain, industry knowledge, glossary, expert experience; stored at .delivery/context/project-background.md). Every role Agent should read it before starting work as the factual basis for domain judgment and deliverables.
tool.context.get_project_background.hint: Project background not recorded yet; guide the user (usually the domain expert) to record it via context.set_project_background before starting work.
Project background recorded; use it as the factual basis for domain judgment and deliverables; suggest updates when it becomes outdated.
tool.context.set_project_background.desc: Set the project background (full overwrite; project-level, shared across tasks). Best maintained by the domain expert: domain overview, core business flows, industry glossary/jargon, constraints/red lines, expert experience. Stored in the .delivery data directory — decoupled from agent templates and unaffected by system upgrades.
tool.context.set_project_background.cont: Full background text (Markdown; suggested sections: domain overview / core flows / glossary / constraints / expert experience)
tool.context.update.description: Update a shared context section (PRD 9.12). Section name like "Unified Language Table" or "5. Unified Language Table".
tool.question.create.description: Create a pending question (PRD 7.9 / 9.13). When blocks_stage is set, the corresponding stage is marked as blocked.
tool.question.create.question: Question content
tool.question.resolve.description: Resolve a pending question (PRD 9.14). Unblocks the stage when no other open question blocks it.
tool.team.get.description: Get project team configuration: member names, emails and roles (one person may hold multiple roles). Returns configured=false when not configured; configure via team.set first.
tool.team.set.description: Add or update a team member (matched by email, roles overwritten). At least one member must be configured before first use. One person may hold multiple roles. Note: before writing, validates that the union of all members' roles covers all 9 roles; otherwise refuses and reports the missing roles.
tool.team.set.name: Member name
tool.team.set.email: Member email (unique key, used for update matching)
tool.team.set.roles_incomplete: Team roles incomplete; must cover all 9 roles: {missing}
tool.user.get.description: Get the current user's personal config (name, email) and the roles matched by email in the project team roster. Returns configured=false when not configured; configure via user.set first.
tool.user.set.description: Set the current user's personal config (name, email). Must be configured before first use. Stored in the user home directory, reused across projects; does not affect the already-configured personal email (email.set). Team role assignment: configure via team.set.
tool.user.set.name: Current user name
tool.user.set.email: Current user email (used to match roles in the team roster)
tool.email.get.description: Get the current user's email notification config (SMTP server, port, encryption, account, sender). The config belongs to the current user, is stored in the user home directory and reused across projects. Password is not returned for security. configured=false when not configured.
tool.email.set.description: Write the current user's email notification config (SMTP, personal level, stored in the user home directory, reused across projects). Only email user + auth code pass needed: host/port/secure/from are auto-filled by email domain or provider (QQ/163/126/yeah/Foxmail/Gmail/Outlook/iCloud supported). host/port can be overridden explicitly. pass is used only for sending and never exposed in the result.
tool.email.set.provider: Email provider key (optional, e.g. qq/163/gmail). Inferred from the email domain when omitted
tool.email.set.host: SMTP server address (optional; filled from provider or domain when omitted)
tool.email.set.port: SMTP port (optional; filled from preset when omitted; required when host is explicitly provided)
tool.email.set.secure: Use TLS/SSL (usually true for port 465, optional)
tool.email.set.pass: SMTP password/auth code (not the login password; enable SMTP in the mail provider first)
tool.email.set.user_not_configured: Configure the current user first via user.set (name, email), then configure the personal email.
tool.email.providers.description: List built-in email provider SMTP presets (host/port/secure and notes on enabling auth codes). For selecting a provider in email.set.
tool.dashboard.hint.commands: Dashboard control: ask the AI to start the dashboard (MCP tools dashboard.start / dashboard.stop / dashboard.status); or via CLI node install.js --dashboard (background start) / --stop-dashboard (stop). Default port 8787, overridable via DELIVERY_DASHBOARD_PORT.
tool.dashboard.start.description: Start the browser task dashboard in the background (detached process, survives the tool call; default port 8787, falls back to a random free port). Idempotent — returns the existing URL when already running. Tell the user the returned url. When asked to start the dashboard, ALWAYS use this tool instead of exploring source code or crafting manual start commands.
tool.dashboard.start.confirm: Reserved parameter (no confirmation needed; the dashboard is read-only and non-destructive)
tool.dashboard.start.hint_started: Dashboard started in the background; tell the user the url to view task progress in the browser.
tool.dashboard.start.hint_already_runnin: Dashboard already running; just tell the user the url.
tool.dashboard.stop.description: Stop the running dashboard process (precise termination by PID, cleans up port records). For old-version dashboards without a PID record, returns a hint to use install.js --stop-dashboard.
tool.dashboard.status.description: Query dashboard status (running / url / port / PID / log path). Use this to check whether the dashboard is up.
tool.update.check.description: Check whether a new version exists on GitHub Releases. Uses a local cache by default (does not re-request GitHub within TTL); pass force=true to force re-request. Silently returns network_error when offline, does not throw. When a new version exists, update manually from the project root: node ~/.config/ai-delivery/delivery-mcp-server/install.js --release.
gate.issue.min_list_items: Section "{section}" has fewer than {min} list items (currently {n})
email.line.question: Question: {q}
email.line.confirmed_recorded: The question you confirmed has been recorded:
email.footer.step1: 1. Open the task dashboard in your browser to view the task: {url}
email.footer.step2: 2. If the dashboard is not running, run in the delivery-mcp-server directory: npm run dashboard (default http://localhost:8787)
email.footer.step3: 3. Or ask an AI assistant to view the task: call task.get (task_id={id})
export.stage_table_header: | Stage | Role | Artifact Type | Status | Artifact ID |
